title: UK balance of payments, Jul-Sep 2026 (ONS, 07:00 London / 02:00 ET) — the quarterly current account, the sterling-relevant half of the 22 December 07:00 stack
source: EST: ons.gov.uk/releases/balanceofpaymentsukjulytoseptember2026, fetched direct 2026-09-09 (HTTP 200, 42,105 bytes) — the ONS release page reads verbatim 'Balance of payments, UK: July to September 2026', 'Release date: 22 December 2026 7:00am', 'This release is not yet published', summary 'A measure of cross-border transactions between the UK and rest of the world. Includes trade, income, capital transfers and foreign assets and liabilities', with the Office for Statistics Regulation accredited-official-statistics statement on the release page itself. Cadence corroborated from the publisher's own JSON bulletin index (api.beta.ons.gov.uk, fetched direct 2026-09-09, HTTP 200): the Q3 edition has printed on 20-23 December in all twelve years 2014-2025 — 2014-12-23, 2015-12-23, 2016-12-23, 2017-12-22, 2018-12-21, 2019-12-20, 2020-12-22, 2021-12-22, 2022-12-22, 2023-12-22, 2024-12-23, 2025-12-22 — and every one of those dates is also a GDP quarterly national accounts date, i.e. the two release together by construction. Filed estimate on this lane's no-self-confirm limit and because market-events-data.ts's confirmed-prefix taxonomy has no slot for the UK Office for National Statistics
notes: PROPOSED BY THE uk-public-sector-finances-2026-12-22 LANE, 2026-09-09, during that event's never-assessed initial research. Why it earns a slot rather than being noted and dropped: the calendar already carries the OTHER two releases in the 22 December 07:00 stack (this lane's own PSF print, and uk-quarterly-national-accounts-2026-12-22 as a proposal from the 09-30 lane), so without this entry the stack reads as two releases when it is three, and the missing one is the one with the clearest sterling channel — the current account is the UK's external financing requirement, the number a gilt or GBP move at 07:00 is most plausibly about. That matters as an ATTRIBUTION control, not as an edge: this lane measured QNA release days at IGLT.L 0.77x an ordinary day (t = -1.87), GBP/USD 0.81x (t = -1.56) and US 10y 0.75x (t = -2.35) across 47 releases since 2014, and the sibling uk-quarterly-national-accounts-2026-09-30 lane independently measured the December editions as the quietest quarter of the four (IGLT.L 0.60x, t = -3.22). Two lanes, two samples, the same direction. Tiered LOW and symbols [] on that measured basis and because this repo tracks no UK-listed name and no house playbook is fiscal-, rates- or sterling-keyed. Estimate widens caution only; nothing date-keyed may act on this.
